title: Name the message
task: Find the flame, flame over circle, corrosion and gas cylinder. Explain one difference between the flame and flame over circle. Then locate the hot-surface warning in the CAT page. Which belongs to a machine warning system rather than a product classification?
answer: Flame concerns specified fire-related hazards; flame over circle identifies oxidizers. Hot surface on the CAT safety page is a machine warning. Exact chemical hazards come from the actual label and SDS.

title: Match the right document
task: Fictional desk records: container label = “Crew Clean A”, supplier = “North Training Supply”; SDS 1 = “Crew Clean B”, same supplier; SDS 2 = “Crew Clean A”, supplier = “West Training Supply”. Neither sheet has been checked against the container. Which sheet is confirmed? What information would you seek before the task?
answer: Neither is confirmed. Obtain the current SDS for the exact product and supplier, compare product identifiers and label information, and resolve any distributor/supplier naming relationship with the responsible person. Do not choose by similar title.

title: Find the section
task: Open the CCOHS SDS sheet. Record which SDS sections address first aid, accidental release, handling/storage, exposure controls/PPE and revision information. Save your answers with the source URL and revision date; close and reopen the file.
answer: Sections 4, 6, 7, 8 and 16 respectively. Source: CCOHS WHMIS—Safety Data Sheet (SDS), revised 28 May 2026. Observe the digital save/reopen action.

title: Keep a count and report a gap
task: Fictional classroom audit: 12 labelled sample cards are supplied. Nine cards have a matching practice SDS; two have the wrong product name; one has no SDS. How many lack a confirmed match? What percentage is that? Write a brief note describing the gap without inventing a product hazard.
answer: 2 + 1 = 3 cards. 3 ÷ 12 × 100 = 25%. Example: “Three of twelve classroom cards lack a confirmed SDS match: two names differ and one sheet is missing. Obtain and verify the correct sheets before using these as product-specific examples.”

title: No symbol is not no hazard
task: A fictional learner says, “There is no diamond, so we can use it.” Use the pictograms sheet to check that statement. Explain your correction to a partner and ask for a check-back.
answer: Some hazard classes/categories require no pictogram. Read the complete label and SDS Section 2 and follow workplace training. The biohazardous infectious materials pictogram also uses a circular border. A partner should restate the need to check the full information.

title: Update a shared briefing
task: Fictional change: the supervisor replaces a practice SDS with a newly verified revision. In pairs, design two ways to make the revision visible on a briefing card. Choose one, test whether another reader can find the date and exact product, revise it and record both contributions. Keep official pictograms unchanged.
answer: Retain both design options, the changed revision record, a reader trial and explained improvement. Each learner contributes and checks the new product/date against the supplied revised document. The exercise does not imply every SDS revision changes the hazard classification.
